title: Vidhura's truth
hook: a dice game, a lost bet, and a minister who won't lie his way free
tomorrow: how many little untruths slip out in one ordinary day?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two views on the kind lie: the empty dipper and the burning house. Sacca: true. Today, truth when it costs the one telling it.

Dice rattle in a cupped hand, then clack across a board. It's the sound of a game night, and in the Jataka it's the sound of a disaster. King Dhananjaya loves to gamble. A stranger arrives, a yakkha named Punnaka, with a magic jewel and a challenge. The king plays, and loses. Punnaka names his prize: your wise minister, Vidhura.
screen: `DICE RATTLE, THEN CLACK.` → `THE KING LOSES.` → `THE PRIZE: VIDHURA.`

segments.voice: The king panics and looks for a way out. Vidhura isn't mine to give, he says. Ask him. So they ask Vidhura, in front of the court. Everyone can see the easy answer: say you're your own man. One sentence, and he walks away safe. Vidhura thinks it through and tells the truth as it stands: he serves the king, so he is the king's to wager. And he goes off with Punnaka, out of the city, into real danger. Why would anyone do that? In the story, his whole life rests on being someone whose word can be trusted, by the king, the court, anyone who asks. One lie to save himself, and every word he'd ever given would be worth less. The tale doesn't end in his death. In the end his wisdom and calm win over even Punnaka, and he comes home. But he didn't know that when he answered. That's what true under pressure is: you answer before you know how it ends. Hear the dice again. Luck runs the game. Vidhura doesn't let luck run his mouth.
screen: `ASK HIM, SAYS THE KING.` · `ONE LIE, AND HE WALKS FREE.` · `HE TELLS THE TRUTH, AND GOES.` · `YOU ANSWER BEFORE IT ENDS.` · then, large: `TRUE UNDER PRESSURE.`

segments.voice: Hold something with some weight in your palm: a coin, a key, a stone. Think of one promise you've made that's due soon, and as you feel the weight, say it to yourself plainly: I said I would, and I will. Then just hold it, steady, while the sit goes on.
Vidhura's truth: telling the truth when it costs you, before you know how the story ends.
Pocket this one: true under pressure, since the dice decide the game but never the answer. Good night.

howItsDone: The Vidhura Jataka is one of the last ten Jataka tales, tied by tradition to the perfection of truthfulness; it is retold in Theravada sermons and is a favorite subject of temple murals.
